summary: Singapore has little land for renewables, so large-scale supply is being built through licensed imports from its neighbours. Corporate buyers can use rooftop PPAs, solar leases and virtual PPAs, and foreign ownership and money transfers are unrestricted.

access.reason: Utility supply comes mainly through licensed imports. EMA gave conditional approvals in 2026, including 900 MW from Johor and 1.3 GW for Sembcorp.

terms.reason: Commercial terms of import licences are not published.

ownership.reason: No general limits on foreign ownership outside a few sectors such as media, and no limits on repatriating earnings or capital.

build.reason: Imports depend on new subsea interconnectors, and the approvals granted so far are conditional.

stability.reason: Import and solar targets are set in official EMA plans, and no retroactive change to renewable contracts was found.

direction.reason: EMA granted further conditional import approvals during 2026, including 1.3 GW for Sembcorp in October.

access.reason: Rooftop PPAs, solar leases and virtual PPAs are all in use, and the national solar target rose to 3 GWp by 2030.

terms.reason: Price and length are agreed between buyer and seller, and surplus solar can be sold through the Enhanced Central Intermediary Scheme.

ownership.reason: No general limits on foreign ownership outside a few sectors, and no limits on repatriating earnings or capital.

build.reason: Dense land use limits how much solar a site can host.

stability.reason: Solar targets have been raised over time, and no retroactive change to solar contracts was found.

direction.reason: The national solar target was raised to 3 GWp by 2030 in March 2026.
